title: Data systems
blurb: Batch and stream processing over many machines, the logs that carry data between systems, and the formats, engines and lakes that store and query it.

main.why: Users write map and reduce, and the runtime partitions the input, schedules tasks and reruns those lost with a machine.

main.title: Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing
main.why: Spark keeps intermediate data in memory and rebuilds a lost partition from its lineage instead of replicating it.
All mappers of a partition write to one shuffle server, which stretched YARN SSD life from about 3 months to 36.

main.title: The Log: What every software engineer should know about real-time data's unifying abstraction
main.why: One append-only, totally ordered log of changes can feed every database, cache and processing system in a company.
Brokers keep no consumer state: consumers pull and track their own offsets, and data flows through the page cache.
At 32 trillion records a day a partition was too heavy to replicate, so Northguard stripes each log into segments.
Watermarks interleave chunked table selects with transaction log events, so a full copy needs no locks and never stalls the log.

main.title: The Dataflow Model
main.why: Windows, watermarks and triggers separate what is computed, where in event time, when results emit and how they refine.

further.title: Discretized Streams: Fault-Tolerant Streaming Computation at Scale

main.title: Apache Flink: Stream and Batch Processing in a Single Engine
main.why: Streams, batch jobs and iterative algorithms all run as pipelined dataflows, with batch treated as a bounded stream.

main.title: State Management in Apache Flink
main.why: Barriers flow through the dataflow and each operator snapshots its state as they pass, giving exactly-once state on recovery.

background.title: Distributed Snapshots: Determining Global States of Distributed Systems

main.why: Kafka transactions commit at each Flink checkpoint and a record UUID dedups downstream, at the cost of 2-minute latency.

main.title: Dremel: Interactive Analysis of Web-Scale Datasets
main.why: Repetition and definition levels store nested records by column, the encoding Parquet later adopted.

further.title: Dremel: A Decade of Interactive SQL Analysis at Web Scale

main.title: Major Technical Advancements in Apache Hive
main.why: ORC swaps RCFile's 4 MB row groups for 256 MB stripes with statistics every 10,000 values, so readers skip what a predicate rules out.
Moving Parquet from Snappy to ZSTD cut storage 39%, and sorting rows by the right columns cut another table 32%.
An external index maps each key to a Parquet file and row, so a point query becomes one ranged read instead of a scan.

main.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores
main.why: A transaction log kept beside the Parquet files in object storage gives ACID tables and time travel without a server.

further.title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics

main.why: Rewriting a 100 TB snapshot on every ingestion left data a day old, so Uber built Hudi for incremental upserts and got it under an hour.
90% of Notion's upserts are updates, which Hudi on S3 absorbs better than Snowflake, saving over a million dollars in 2022.
One SQL engine reads Hive, key-value stores and other sources through connectors, with compute apart from storage.
Data in S3, compute in elastic virtual warehouses and a shared metadata service, each scaled on its own.
Redshift kept its code-generating MPP engine but moved storage to S3 and added concurrency scaling and serverless.

main.title: Druid: A Real-time Analytical Data Store
main.why: Real-time nodes serve fresh events from memory and historical nodes serve immutable column segments, for sub-second queries on billions of rows.

further.title: Pinot: Realtime OLAP for 530 Million Users

main.title: ClickHouse: Lightning Fast Analytics for Everyone
main.why: MergeTree tables write sorted parts and merge them in the background, and queries run vectorized in the style of X100.
